label: Constitutional Analysis
sentences: The question here falls under Article II, Section 3. The President gives Congress information of the state of the Union and recommends measures to it; on extraordinary occasions he may convene both houses or either of them, and if they disagree about the time of adjournment he may adjourn them to such time as he thinks proper; he receives ambassadors and other public ministers, takes care that the laws be faithfully executed, and commissions all the officers of the United States.
This story is about the executive answering comments in litigation on a proposed judgment.

On June 1, 1787 Wilson told the Convention that "The only powers he conceived strictly Executive were those of executing the laws, and appointing officers, not appertaining to and appointed by the Legislature."
From George Washington, Proclamation of Sept. 25: “to take care that the laws be faithfully executed.”
The United States claims the proposed Final Judgment will remedy the antitrust violations.
The strongest argument against this is that answering comments on a proposed judgment lets the executive shape the remedy beyond bare execution.
We read this clause to mean that work in litigation executes an existing law and is not lawmaking.
